root_idea.summary: The root centers on obtaining or experiencing good without hardship, trouble, or harmful consequence.
root_idea.development: This orientation develops into meanings of pleasant and wholesome food, enjoyable provision, gifts and nourishment, and finding beneficial herbage. The tar term may be associated with healing; the expression for a portion of the night is explicitly treated as outside the main semantic branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested nominal form normalized to the Classical Arabic citation form هَنِيءٌ.

senses.definition: Pleasant and easy to enjoy, without hardship or harmful consequence; wholesome.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran it occurs in the accusative form هَنِيئًا with food, drink, or provision being consumed or enjoyed, including the construction هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا, emphasizing both enjoyment and a wholesome result.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come or happen without inconvenience; to be pleasant, enjoyable, easy to swallow, or free from harmful consequence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of food, things, or events that bring enjoyment without trouble; the same pleasantness may be expressed as something pleasing to a person, including pleasing news.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of livestock, to feed on good herbage and, in related usage, to become satiated with food or herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: هَنْأَى specifically describes camels that have found good herbage but are not yet satiated; other attestations describe eating or becoming satiated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rejoice in someone or something.
To make something pleasant or enjoyable to someone; to cause someone to enjoy it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject may be God, health, or another cause of enjoyment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed someone or give him to eat.
To give or bestow something, especially plentifully.
To make food good by properly preparing or seasoning it.
To put one's property into a right or good state.
To nourish or maintain people, satisfy their wants, and provide for them.
To aid, succour, or defend someone.
To smear camels with hināʾ, a tar or liquid pitch, as a remedy or preservative against mange or scab.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated material is called هِنَاءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A formula of congratulation wishing someone joy in a favorable matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions such as لِيَهْنِئْكَ الفَارِسُ, literally wishing that the horseman give the person joy, and applied to congratulating someone on the horseman's exploits.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone think of pleasant things or desired objects; to grant him enjoyment in something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One reported usage concerns pleasant and desired thoughts intruding into prayer; when God is the agent, the sense is to grant enjoyment in the thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To congratulate someone on an achievement, possession, or other favorable matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The associated formula is لِيَهْنِئْكَ, ‘may it give you joy.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give many gifts.
To pride oneself on something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This use is reported with a qualification that it may be a mistaken form for تَهَيَّأَ, but it is retained as an attributed lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone for aid, succour, or defence.
To ask someone for a gift.
To concede or give someone a portion of his dues or rights.
A gift.
A portion of the night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized use explicitly treated as outside the root's main semantic branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of smearing with hināʾ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun associated with smearing camels with tar or liquid pitch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tar or liquid pitch, or a kind of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as the substance with which camels are smeared.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A raceme of a palm tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Cited as a dialectal variant of إِهَانٌ or a form produced from it by transposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something that comes or happens without inconvenience; an unalloyed gratification.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader Classical use describes a favorable occurrence or received benefit; Quranic consumption and provision are represented separately under the Quranic form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An optative expression wishing that something be enjoyed without trouble and produce a wholesome result.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in formulas such as هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا and هَنِيئًا لَهُ ذَلِكَ, often with an understood verb of wishing, eating, or drinking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A little; a little while.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Related variant forms are also reported, including هُنَيَّةٌ and هُنَيْهَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A servant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence qualifies this as a reported reading in a traditional expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A giver, nourisher, or provider of people's wants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This interpretation is tied to a disputed reading and to the idea that the person so named gives, nourishes, or maintains others.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unalloyed gratification; what is pleasant and free from harmful consequence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions wishing or assigning pleasant enjoyment to someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel smeared with hināʾ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Hināʾ is the tar or liquid pitch used in the treatment or preservation of camels.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Verb of coming or happening without inconvenience.
Variant formulation of the food-pleasant sense.
Making a thing pleasant to someone.
Enjoyable food with no harmful result.
Livestock finding good herbage without satiation.
A cause such as health making something pleasant.
Maintaining people and satisfying their wants.
Making pleasant or desired thoughts occur.
Qualified use meaning to pride oneself.
Conceding or giving a share of rights.
The act of smearing with hināʾ.
Specialized adjective for camels not yet satiated.
Dialectal or transposed term for a palm raceme.
Quranic pleasant-wholesome sense and broader event/benefit use.
Pleasant and harmless to the eater.
Explanation of giver, nourisher, and provider.
Passive participle for a camel smeared with hināʾ.

cautions: The Quranic form group contains inflected accusative occurrences normalized here under the citation form هَنِيءٌ.
The servant reading under هَانِئٌ, the pride sense of تَهَنَّأَ, and the palm-raceme sense of هِنَاءٌ are retained with the qualifications stated in their usage conditions.
The expression هِنْءٌ for a portion of the night is retained as a specialized use, although the root-level evidence explicitly places it outside the main semantic branch.
